cues: The ethoxide ion is a strong nucleophile, rich in electrons.
It attacks the carbon carrying the iodine, and it must come in from the side exactly opposite the iodine.
This is the S N two mechanism you met in haloalkanes.
text: Why does this work? The ethoxide ion is a strong nucleophile, rich in electrons. It attacks the carbon carrying the iodine, and it must come in from the side exactly opposite the iodine. This is the S N two mechanism you met in haloalkanes.
